challenges.finding: Publisher reports community resistance blocking safe burials in one Nord-Ubangi zone and slowing decontamination in Isiro; a mobility problem preventing burials in the other Nord-Ubangi zone; in Nord-Ubangi no fixed water point or dedicated latrines and showers at one site, insufficient protective materials and no triage at another; in Bas-Uele laboratory overheating, no cold chain and no computers or connectivity, and a marked slowdown of psychosocial support; in Tshopo a near-stockout of laboratory consumables and a need for more motorcycles; and in Nord-Kivu one control point out of service after a security incident. Nord-Kivu reports 55 of 59 rings opened (93.2%), 22 of 23 health facilities decontaminated (95.7%) and 10 of 32 households given targeted disinfection. No intervention effect is established.

It prints a cumulative of 4 828 people vaccinated; the cumulative rises by exactly the 458 doses, consistent with one dose per person, which the page does not state; compassionate use and the study are mixed in these counts. Priority groups are front-line workers and contacts; no split is printed. Reconciles with SR188: 4 370 + 458 = 4 828 people and 1 129 - 458 = 671 doses remaining of 5 500 received. The remaining stock is one dose below 5 500 - 4 828, consistent with the 1 dose lost printed in SR187; SR189 prints no loss count. No coverage or denominator is printed. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations; there is no national total. The SitRep does not name the vaccine product.

Tshopo counts people vaccinated (14 823 in cumulative). The 99.1% provincial coverage and the zone coverages (Kabondo 57.6%, Mangobo 76.1%) are printed without a denominator; INSP prints none in this edition (SR186 printed a target of 14 960 for an earlier 95.1%), and none is carried. 1 544 adverse events following immunisation, printed as minor and mainly body and injection-site pain. No daily count or dose stock is printed. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations; there is no national total. The SitRep does not name the vaccine product.

Haut-Uele counts people vaccinated (3 388: 1 827 men and 1 561 women) out of a pre-registered group of 4 428. INSP prints a coverage of 77% without naming its denominator; it matches 3 388 of the 4 428 pre-registered (76.5%), so it is not a population coverage. Count and stock continue from SR187 (2 653 + 735 = 3 388 people; 1 447 - 735 = 712 doses left of the same 4 100); SR188 printed no Haut-Uele line, so the 735 spans two report days and no daily count is derived. 3 388 of 4 100 doses received were used, leaving 712 across 7 health zones. No daily count is printed. SR186 and SR187 printed a pre-registered group of 3 300 front-line workers with 2 485 and 2 653 vaccinated; the group has changed, so no same-group trend is inferred. Not comparable with other provinces' rows, which count different populations; there is no national total. The SitRep does not name the vaccine product.

challenges: Publisher reports community resistance blocking safe burials in one Nord-Ubangi zone and slowing decontamination in Isiro; a mobility problem preventing burials in the other Nord-Ubangi zone; in Nord-Ubangi no fixed water point or dedicated latrines and showers at one site, insufficient protective materials and no triage at another; in Bas-Uele laboratory overheating, no cold chain and no computers or connectivity, and a marked slowdown of psychosocial support; in Tshopo a near-stockout of laboratory consumables and a need for more motorcycles; and in Nord-Kivu one control point out of service after a security incident. Nord-Kivu reports 55 of 59 rings opened (93.2%), 22 of 23 health facilities decontaminated (95.7%) and 10 of 32 households given targeted disinfection. No intervention effect is established.

Sud-Ubangi prints a new 148/148 after 47 days without a new case; it is kept as printed with no same-cohort change inferred. The lowest printed rate is Haut-Uele (77.4%).
